statement: S102/S103: decisions about the requirements a request states (bound, force) and how they combine (intersection, contradiction, alternatives, other objects), under the shared precedence policy. These programs conclude requirement states only, never product facts.

vocabulary.name: reading
vocabulary.meaning: a reader of the request found this bound for the requirement: reader 'local' (the request-constraint reader) or 'shared' (the quantity knowledge's bound words, also used to read documents) (one bound per reader)

vocabulary.name: space
vocabulary.meaning: the requirement is said of an available space (a cupboard, an opening): what must fit is at most its size

vocabulary.name: range_inferred
vocabulary.meaning: a bare range with no bound word: the bound is inferred from the kind (a presumption only)

vocabulary.name: stated_limit
vocabulary.meaning: S102 input of RQ08 (superseded in S103): a requirement stated for this criterion with this value

vocabulary.name: claim
vocabulary.meaning: the evidence supports this value of this field (S100 decision predicate)

vocabulary.name: limit_conflict
vocabulary.meaning: S102 conclusion of RQ08 (superseded in S103): two different limits for one criterion

vocabulary.name: stated_bound
vocabulary.meaning: the request states the limit with a bound word or 'between' (an explicit limit, not a bare quantity)

vocabulary.name: hedge
vocabulary.meaning: a preference word governs the requirement's phrase ('ideally', 'preferably', 'possibly', 'if possible', 'would be nice')

vocabulary.name: corrected_by
vocabulary.meaning: a later statement of the request replaces this requirement ('actually', 'make it', 'I mean'), for the same property and object

vocabulary.name: mandatory
vocabulary.meaning: the requirement's force was decided as a requirement (not a preference, not superseded)

vocabulary.name: preference
vocabulary.meaning: the requirement's force was decided as a preference

vocabulary.name: frame
vocabulary.meaning: what the requirement constrains: the property, the object (the product to buy, or another one the request mentions) and the scenario it belongs to ('base', or a scenario the request introduces with 'or', 'if', 'when')

vocabulary.name: limit
vocabulary.meaning: one end of the requirement's interval: side low or high, the value in the criterion's base unit, closure inclusive or strict

vocabulary.name: same_frame
vocabulary.meaning: two different requirements on the same property, object and scenario

vocabulary.name: empty
vocabulary.meaning: the low end of a is above the high end of b (or equal with a strict end): no value satisfies both

vocabulary.name: contradiction
vocabulary.meaning: two mandatory requirements on one frame that no value can satisfy together

vocabulary.name: combines
vocabulary.meaning: two mandatory requirements on one frame that hold together: the product must satisfy both (their intersection)

vocabulary.name: alternative
vocabulary.meaning: two mandatory requirements on one property and object in different scenarios: only the bound shared by every scenario is certain

vocabulary.name: other_object
vocabulary.meaning: two requirements on one property of different objects: never combined, never contradictory

vocabulary.name: violation
vocabulary.meaning: a preference was turned into a mandatory requirement (must never hold)

programs.statement: S103 (owner review of S102, RQ08): how the requirements of one request combine. Requirements on one property, object and scenario hold together (their intersection); an empty intersection is a contradiction (asked); different scenarios are alternatives (only what every scenario requires is certain); different objects never combine. The interval arithmetic itself (intersection, the stricter end, the hull of alternatives) is algorithmic and stays in code.

exclusive.why: two requirements cannot both contradict each other and hold together
requirements in one scenario are not alternatives of each other
requirements on one object are not about different objects
alternatives are scenarios of one object

abstains.inclusive: An inclusive end needs no rule of its own: equal inclusive ends are compatible (exactly that value), and ends that cross are covered by RC02.

history.note: S102: first request decision program (bound of a requirement, conflicting limits).

S103: RQ08 reclassified (owner decision) and superseded by request_combination (RC01-RC10); force of a limit (RQ09-RQ11); contests name rules; keys on single-valued inputs; closure and intent vocabulary as data; admission records for every rule that runs. RQ01/RQ02 superseded by RQ03/RQ04 (one bound reader, qk.2.5).

closure.statement: S103: whether the limit itself satisfies a requirement. Keyed by the bound phrase the readers report; a phrase not listed is inclusive (the cautious reading for a buyer: it never excludes a product at the limit) and is reported as such.

intent.statement: S103: words that change the force or the frame of a limit. Vocabulary data, read by src/phase253_request_constraints.ts; each list is evidence for one input fact of request_requirements or request_combination.
intent.otherObjectNote: Read only when an earlier limit of the same property exists (two objects contrasted); 'another air fryer' alone describes the purchase, not a second object.
